pairs.difference: A: the cap board is soft satin blue with slightly raised corners, and the cord and tassel have a quiet sheen, close to the soft finish of the real cards. B: the hat cone and brim are one seamless charcoal rubber with a dusty airbrushed falloff and no felt nap or brim stitching. The purple band and yellow buckle have the same soft clay finish, so metal, cloth and felt do not separate.
pairs.fix: Make the hat look like felt with very fine, quiet nap. Add a thin stitched line along the brim edge, a woven look on the band, and a small sharp highlight on a metal buckle. Keep the felt matte.

pairs.difference: A: the cauldron has a sandy, grainy highlight on the belly and a crisp rim, and the green liquid has sharp glassy bubbles. This speckled matte coating is more textured and more contrasted between materials than the lessons' real cards. B: the gloves are soft, blurred red leather with broad gentle highlights and fine creases at the thumb, like the real glove's softness, although they have no stitching.
pairs.fix: Remove the speckled grain from the cauldron belly. Paint the iron as smooth dark metal with a soft, broad highlight. Soften the bubble edges slightly.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is soft, smooth red with no weave but gentle folds, and the badge has a clean metal rim. B: the broom bristles are thick glossy strands like clay noodles, enlarged into chunky toy detail, and the red binding is fat cord. The handle is an evenly polished tube with no wood grain.
pairs.fix: Draw the bristles as many thin dry straw fibres with a matte finish. Add fine quiet wood grain to the handle and keep its highlight soft and narrow.

pairs.difference: A: the envelope is matte paper with soft creases, and the photos have a slight sheen and fine small-scale painted detail. B: the wheel has fine quiet wood grain and a mid-gloss varnish, with a polished brass hub that separates clearly from the wood. Both keep a real matte-versus-shiny range and neither shows smear or chunky detail. A's high gloss and detail numbers come from the small busy picture, not from a false material.

A: every brass part, from stem to arms and base, is the same wet, saturated gold with crisp streak highlights, so it reads as lacquered and uniform (gloss 0.193, above the real range). Only the wax is matte. B: the brass is softer and browner with broader highlights, and the frosted chimney gives a clear change of material, with a softer overall finish.
pairs.fix: Lower the gold shine. Make the brass a slightly worn, muted metal with broad soft highlights and a few darker satin areas. Give the candles dull waxy tops.

pairs.difference: A: the glass, ice and umbrella are built from clean flat translucent layers with simple pale highlight bands. The surfaces stay quiet. B: the mist inside the ball is made of wispy feathered streaks with a smeary airbrushed look and scattered sparkles. The glass shell has little real reflection, and the brass stand is a generic glossy gold.
pairs.fix: Replace the feathered streaks with a smooth soft mist with few marks. Give the glass a clean window reflection and a thin bright rim. Make the stand a duller brass.

pairs.difference: A: the walls are clay-like stone with outlined raised blocks scattered across them, the roof has puffy rounded shingles, and the sills and frames share one soft waxy finish. The glowing windows have crisp edges. Stone, roof and wood have the same surface. B: the lighthouse has soft white plaster bricks, a satin red rail and a smooth glass lantern, with quiet, low-contrast joints that match the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the blocks flatter with thin, quiet mortar lines. Make the stone matte and slightly rough, and the roof slates thin and hard-edged. Keep the wall, roof and sill finishes visibly different.

pairs.difference: A: the cat's body has an even, fine sandy or felt-like grain across the whole surface, so it reads as flocked clay instead of fur, and the same noise covers it from head to tail. Only the eyes and bell are shiny. B: the fountain has smooth pale stone with soft edges, and clear blue water streams with gentle highlights. The surfaces are soft and quiet, like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Remove the sandy noise from the body. Paint short soft fur clumps along the back, chest and tail, with a soft sheen on the head and back. Keep the coat smooth at small scale.

pairs.difference: A: dense, even wood-grain lines and knots cover the lid, the cross and the sides at the same contrast, like a decorative printed pattern over a semi-varnished surface, so the grain is more insistent than the quiet grain on the real barrel. B: the table has matte stone with a few thin cracks and satin board squares, so its surfaces differ clearly. The drawn cracks look a little decorative, but they are sparse.
pairs.fix: Make the wood grain finer and fainter, with only a few long lines per plank and no knots on the lid. Leave larger smooth areas and keep the finish satin.

pairs.difference: A: the tombstone is smooth, soft grey putty with evenly scattered small pits and a clean cartoon crack, so it looks like moulded clay rather than cut stone. The moss is a lumpy sponge with uniform stippling. B: the shoes have varied finishes, with fine perforated mesh, glossy rubber soles, matte upper panels and shiny laces, all small in scale. Its gloss and detail values sit at the top of the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the stone hard and chipped, with fine irregular surface wear and crisp worn edges instead of evenly spaced pits. Draw the moss as fine, small, soft tufts.

pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin has a waxy lacquer with scattered dark pits, crisp incised outlines around the face cuts and a painted glow along each edge. The skin carries more applied detail than a real card and its micro texture is low for the group. B: the duck is uniform moulded yellow plastic with soft broad highlights and a dull metal spring, which suits its subject and matches the soft finish of the real cards.
pairs.fix: Remove the speckled pits and the sharp cut outlines. Give the skin a soft, even waxy surface with broad gentle highlights, and show thickness in the carved flesh with a soft pale inner edge.

pairs.difference: A: the balloons are smooth, airbrushed latex with a small round soft highlight, which suits the material, and the numbers are low because there is little surface detail on them. B: the buoy is a plain, soft red surface with thin rims and a glossier gold bell, and the metal has a soft blurred finish. Both have the soft, quiet finish of the real cards, with no noise or smear to separate them.

pattern: Generated cards still show themselves in the surface. Finish is too uniform: one clay, wax or lacquer skin runs across parts that should differ, or one even noise or pit pattern covers the whole object (cat body, tombstone, cauldron highlight). Surface detail is applied evenly and is too insistent: dense wood grain, outlined blocks, scattered pits, drawn cracks. Metal is over-saturated wet gold with crisp streak highlights. Thin materials are enlarged into chunky toy forms, such as noodle bristles. Real cards are softer and quieter, with low-contrast joints and fine grain, broad gentle highlights, and clear changes between matte and shiny parts.
